ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are three soft magnetic material rods; M is located above, P is a horizontal rod at the lower left, and a solenoid coil is wound around P; O is a horizontal rod on the right side and is not connected into the circuit. The two ends of the coil are connected by wires to the battery and switch K at the bottom. In the battery symbol, the longer plate on the right side indicates the positive electrode; the positive electrode is connected to the right-side wire and to the right end of the coil, and switch K is in the lower left branch. Reasoning: After switch K is closed, according to the conventional current direction, the current starts from the positive electrode on the right side of the battery, goes upward along the right-side wire into the right end of the coil, then passes through the solenoid according to the winding direction shown in the figure, and finally goes downward from the left end of the coil along the left-side wire, returning through the closed switch to the negative electrode of the battery. According to the winding method of the coil in the figure, observed from the left end of P, the current in the coil circulates counterclockwise. According to the solenoid end-face determination rule: if the current is counterclockwise when viewed from one end, then that end is the N pole. Therefore, the left end of P becomes the N pole.

After K closes, take conventional current from the battery's positive long plate on the right, up the right side, through the solenoid winding as drawn, and down the left side. Looking at the left end of P, the current around that end is anticlockwise. By the end rule for a solenoid, the anticlockwise-current end is the north pole. Therefore the left end of P becomes N.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram and current path after switch K is closed: conventional current leaves the right-hand positive battery terminal, rises to the right end of the coil on P, follows the helical turns as drawn, and returns by the left lead. Apply the right-hand screw/grip rule to the current circulation in the coil to find that the magnetic field inside the solenoid, along rod P, is directed toward the left.
